aboutMore: (second about me. read it at normal speed. i'm doing it for you.) i took piano for 8 years with mrs albrecht (tuesdays, her living room smells like cough drops) and that's where i learned bpm: she made me play with a metronome until i could feel it in my teeth. my mom works second shift (3 to 11), so i get the evenings to myself: a subwoofer under my bed, an old upright in the basement and one patient fish named Reverb. i also run sound for the school musical (headset, black shirt, 'standby' is my favorite word). there's exactly one song i have never sped up. it's not on my page. it's for my grandma june. UNTZ (but gently).

blog.title: the one song i leave alone
blog.body: i speed up everything. the school bell. the dial-up. silence (still working on it). there is one song i don't touch. it's clair de lune and it's 5 minutes at normal speed on our old upright in the basement. mrs albrecht taught it to me in 7th grade. my grandma june, who lives with us, sits on the basement stairs with her tea while i play it. she doesn't say anything. she did this when i was 9 and she still does. last week i missed a note in the middle and she said 'that's the one.' i said what. she said 'that note. keep it.' so now i play it with the wrong note on purpose. it's the best version. it's the only song i'd never nightcore. it's the one i'd keep at exactly this speed forever. (UNTZ. but quietly. like a heartbeat.)

blog.title: tech week (a person in black in the dark)
blog.body: tech week for the fall musical. i'm on sound. there are 4 of us on crew and we all wear black and use headsets and say 'standby' like it's a sacred word. my job: 47 cues. every door slam, every phone ring, every 'ding' when somebody on stage has an idea. cue 47 is the final chord. it's one button, 11 seconds, and i have waited my whole life for a button like that. on opening night thad (he has a monologue) lost his line and the whole room waited and i hit cue 31 half a second early and covered for him with a thunderclap. he was supposed to speak after the thunder. he did. nobody knew. i have never felt so fast and so still at the same time. after, thad found me and said 'you saved my life.' i said 'it was a thunderclap.' he said 'it was a SAVE.' he cried a little. i think i love tech.

blog.title: what the fridge says (a gina consultation)
blog.body: gina (ghosthunter_gina) sent me 40 seconds from her 'Under Review' pile, the 3 hours of auditorium audio she hasn't explained yet (the other 11 hours are the fridge, she knows, it's a control). she said 'listen for the voice.' i listened at 1x, at 1.5x (obviously) and at 0.5x. there's a sigh at 0:22. it's the fridge compressor kicking on: the hum slides up a few cents and settles. 60 hertz. a B-flat, a little flat. it sounds like somebody trying. i told gina. she was quiet for a minute. then she said 'so the Under Review pile is the fridge too.' i said 'it's all the fridge. but the fridge has feelings.' she said 'i can work with that.' i tuned the basement piano to it. it sounds almost like the room i was born in. gina's renamed the pile. it's called 'The B-Flat That Stays.'

blog.title: mom knows about the subwoofer
blog.body: so the thing i've been hiding for 8 months is a subwoofer under my bed. today i found a sticky note on the carpet next to it. it said 'honey, please keep it under 11. love, mom. p.s. i can feel it in the kitchen. i don't mind. it feels like a heartbeat in the house.' she's known the whole time. she works second shift, 3 to 11, and she told me she comes home and sits in the dark kitchen and feels the floor go UNTZ and it means i'm home and ok. malten i was SO ready to fight about this. i had a speech. it was 14 bpm of rebuttal. i have no use for it now. i turned the volume to 10. i put a sticky note back on her door: 'ok. love, nikki. p.s. UNTZ.'
